previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for fever, cough, and shortness of breath, with lab evidence of infection and clinical signs of sepsis. She was treated for suspected bacterial pneumonia and COPD exacerbation, receiving IV antibiotics and a steroid taper. Her symptoms improved rapidly, with normalization of white blood cell count and stable oxygenation. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics, a prednisone taper, and her baseline medications, with instructions to monitor weight and symptoms. Blood cultures remained pending at discharge, and follow-up was arranged for INR monitoring and leg assessment.

#Somnolence- Pt was noted to be lethargic in the setting of high

consequences of not going to the ICU. On a regimen that was half 
the dose of her home methadone and gabapentin patient remained 
consistenty alert until the end of her hospitalization.

and signs with imaging consistent with volume overload. She was 
diuresed aggressively with IV medications and transitioned to 
home lasix until clinical improvement. She was weaned down to 1L 
O2 and will go home with home oxygen for ambulatory O2 sat 
requirements.

ED for suspected pneumonia, however clinically she does did not 
display signs of infection throughout her hospitalization.

time course, food poisoning is possible. Viral gastroenteritis 
also possible. Patient appears to have chronic diarrhea likely 
secondary to HIV meds.
